conviction_note: Q3 is a fresh, un-pre-released quarter with no numeric company guide and no sourceable consensus. Q2's record result, a full quarter of the chartered Normand Jarstein on the 2+1-year Black Sea contract, Reach Remote 1 booked by Equinor through Q3, a weak Q3 2025 comparison (NOK 688m / EBIT 51m) and healthy peer Q3s (DOF, Eidesvik) all point to a year-on-year beat. Against that, the stock has lagged its peers by about 10 points since late September on the Statnett claim and the SAFE strike, which a Q4 comment could add to. The bar is unsourced, so every finding is capped small and p_up sits at 55. abs_move is the new-numbers base on a thin $0.12m/day name with a 6.1% median reaction. Findings sum to +0.9, and the scaled number is (2*0.55-1)*8 = +0.8; the two agree because both rest on the same weak lean.

findings.finding: Q3 2026 was set up to be far stronger than the weak Q3 2025 comparison (revenue NOK 688m, EBIT NOK 51m). Three things support that: a full quarter of the Normand Jarstein charter on the signed 2+1-year Black Sea IMR contract (Q2 had it only from mid-May), Equinor call-offs booking most of Reach Remote 1's capacity through Q2 and Q3, and a record Q2 exit (EBIT NOK 192.4m, backlog NOK 1.85bn, +61% y/y).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose 9.7% on the Q2 2026 'strong results' print (2026-08-18) and 9.9% on Q1 2025's record quarter. It fell 6-7% on each weak print from Q3 2025 to Q1 2026. It moves with the size of the EBIT surprise both ways
findings.why_not_priced: No sourceable consensus exists for Q3, and coverage is about four analysts on a $0.12m/day name. The stock has fallen from 6.69 (22 Sep) to 5.89 while DOF and Subsea7 fell only ~4%, so the price is not discounting a strong quarter. If it were, REACH would have held its post-Q2 level of about 6.6 like its peers.
findings.independence: Black Sea contract and Normand Jarstein charter: https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=674328 (2026-05-22). Q2 backlog and new vessel from mid-May: https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=680029

findings.finding: The SAFE strike escalated on 20 Oct from 6 to 11 members, and staff were laid off (permittert) because of it, so there was an operational hit in Q4. The company never disclosed the escalation on NewsWeb. SAFE says the strike was suspended from 15 Nov while members vote on a new offer, deadline 26 Nov; it could resume no earlier than 1 Dec. The release will have to address the Q4 cost.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior strike at this company in the history. The stock rose 2.6% on 16 Nov, the first session after the suspension post, against flat peers (DOF -0.4%, SUBC -0.3%), so the suspension looks partly priced
findings.original_quote: "Alle som er tatt ut i streik, samt de som er permittert som følge av streiken, går dermed tilbake i arbeid fra og med 15. november 2026." (All those taken out on strike, and those laid off as a result of the strike, return to work from 15 November 2026.) And from 20 Oct: "Fra og med i dag ble ytterligere 5 medlemmer i Reach Subsea tatt ut i streik. Konflikten omfatter nå totalt 11 medlemmer." (From today a further 5 members were taken out on strike. The conflict now covers 11 members in total.)
findings.why_not_priced: Only the union's Norwegian site carries the escalation, the layoffs and the suspension; the company has issued no update since 19 Oct. The 16 Nov uptick prices the suspension but not a quantified Q4 cost. If a cost were priced, the stock would not have outperformed peers on 16 Nov.
findings.independence: The company's own start-of-strike notice: https://api3.oslo.oslobors.no/v1/newsreader/message?messageId=684262. Escalation post: https://safe.no/opptrapping-og-streikemarkering-utenfor-hovedkontoret-til-reach-subsea/ (2026-10-20). Same union as source, so not fully independent

findings.finding: Statnett's claim of up to NOK 158.5m plus interest (about 8% of market cap at NOK 5.89 x 327.4m shares) over a conditional cable-installation tender. The company rejects it as without merit. The Q3 report will show whether any provision is taken.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock fell 3.5% on 9 Nov (the notice came at 20:15 CET, after the close) and 2.1% on 10 Nov, while DOF rose 2.1% and 2.2% and SUBC rose 4.3% then fell 0.8%. Roughly 7-9 points of underperformance over two sessions, so it is largely priced
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced (see the reaction). The residual is a provision decision the company has not stated; a provision would make it an EBIT or finance hit in the report, and no provision would mean a contingent-liability note only. Sized as a below-operating-income one-off with no path to the guide.
findings.independence: Price reaction from https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/REACH.OL?range=6mo&interval=1d against DOFG.OL and SUBC.OL

findings.finding: The Viking Reach sale completed on 26 Oct as previously communicated. The Q3 report's subsequent events should confirm ~NOK 70m of Q4 gains and >NOK 200m of liquidity against NOK 369.9m of remaining Reach Remote 3/4 capex.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No visible reaction to the 26 Oct completion (6.14 to 6.12). The MoA on 4 Aug came while the stock was drifting ahead of Q2
findings.why_not_priced: It is almost entirely priced, because the company guided it; the residual is confirmation that liquidity funds the newbuild programme without equity. Sized toward 0 because it lands inside what was guided.

findings.finding: Peer Q3s published on 12 Nov show a steady subsea market: DOF utilisation 86% (87%), EBITDA ex-gains +13% y/y, backlog USD 7.0bn; Eidesvik fleet utilisation 97%.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No measured history of REACH reacting to peer prints
findings.why_not_priced: A sector proxy, so weak: DOF was flat on its print, and REACH's utilisation story is idiosyncratic (Q1 2026 was terrible in the same market). Filed small as macro-to-company transmission.

findings.finding: Into the print the stock has lagged its listed subsea peers by about 10 points: REACH 6.69 to 5.89 (-12%) from 22 Sep to 16 Nov, against DOF -4.4% and SUBC -4.3%. The 20-day and 60-day run-ups (-1.0% / -2.0%) hide this, so expectations are depressed going into a seasonally strong quarter.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Similar set-up before Q2 2026: the stock drifted to 5.35-5.5 and rose 9.7% on the print. Before Q3 2025 and Q1 2026 it drifted and still fell on weak prints
findings.why_not_priced: It is a price fact, so it is by definition 'in the price'. The claim is that it lowers the bar, which is an inference; the Statnett claim and strike account for part of it.

baseline_tension: The findings lean mildly positive while the sealed lean is ~0 and the 20-day run-up is flat. The 10-point underperformance against peers since September is negative sentiment the free control does not see, and the findings argue it sets a low bar rather than signalling informed selling.
language_note: The SAFE union's Norwegian site (safe.no) carried the strike's escalation to 11 members on 20 Oct, the layoffs ('permittert som følge av streiken') and the 14 Nov suspension pending a ballot due 26 Nov. The company's own filings are bilingual (Q3 2025 and Q1/Q2 2026 headlines issued in both Norwegian and English) and carried nothing the English versions did not
